newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador telecom chief quits ahead of privatization.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador telecom chief quits ahead of privatization.

text.p: Ecuador's Finance Minister Pablo Concha announced Thursday the resignation of the head of state telephone company Emetel, ahead of the partial privatization which kicks off next week.

News that Emetel head Manuel Zhindon had quit came hours after the National Council for Modernization (Conam), in charge of sell-offs, said the prospectus for the sale of 35 percent of Emetel would be ready next week, costing $30,000.
"Next week Conam will call the international tender via the sale of the prospectus. Five international operators will take part," Conam head Leonardo Escobar told reporters.
U.S. firms MCI and GTE, Italy's Stet, Spain's Telefonica and Korea Telecom all signed up for the Emetel privatization process last November.

The Ecuadorean government hopes to raise $1.0 billion from the partial sale of Emetel, which is valued at $4.0 billion. Conditions include installing 2.5 million local lines, making $2.5 billion a year in profits and giving the company international operations.
Ecuador's 11.7 million inhabitants have one of the lowest telephone "densities" in Latin America, with just seven lines for every 100 people.
